newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: SHARP TO WORK WITH UNIONS ON MARITIME REFORM
Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp, says the Government will discuss the recommendations of a report into the shipping industry with maritime unions.
The report, compiled by a group of senior shipping executives, calls for lower labour costs and Government initiatives to stimulate industry growth.
It also advocates a second register of ships, which would operate under more lenient tax and labour laws.
Unions are opposed to the changes, but Mr Sharp says they're prepared to work with the Government to come up with workable reforms which will give the industry a solid future.
CELEBS BACK INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS ON WIK
A so-called prominant citizens statement, signed by more than 100 people, threatens protest action at the Sydney Olympics if the Government doesn't uphold the High Court's native title ruling.
Signatories include Oscar winner, Geoffrey Rush; actor Judy Davis; QC Hal Wooten; Jewish leader Mark Leibler and footballer Des Hasler.
The group says the Prime Minister must show leadership on the issue, rather than buckling to political pressure to oppose the ruling, which recognised native title on pastoral leases.
Meanwhile, ATSIC Social Justice Commissioner, Mick Dodson, says a populist political campaign is being waged against the Wik decison, in place of what should be a debate about property rights.
Mr Dodson says people like Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, are spreading outrageous misinformation.
PM'S WIK PLAN "MORE DAMAGING THAN STOLEN GENERATION"
ATSIC Social Justice Commissioner, Mick Dodson, says the Prime Minister's 10-point native title plan is the single biggest act of dispossession in Australia's 200 year colonial history.
Mr Dodson says the plan will have the same effect as the removal of indigenous children from their families, under a scheme which produced what's become known as the stolen generation.
He says John Howard's Wik response will further dispossess Aboriginal people of their land.
DANGER OF LIMESTONE CLIFF WHICH KILLED 9 "NOT KNOWN"

A Conservation and Land Management officer has told the inquest into the Gracetown tragedy in Western Australia, he had no previous knowledge about the danger of a cliff which collapsed, killing nine people.

The lawyer representing the families of the victims yesterday produced a letter the Mines Department sent to the National Park Authority warning of the dangers of a limestone cliff in Gracetown in 1984 - 12 yeras before last September's landslide.
CALM officer, Robert Klok, said the letter did not refer to the ledge that collapsed, but to another cliff some 300 metres away which was levelled with explosives.
Mr Klok said at the time he examined the entire beach at Gracetown and did not believe any other cliffs in the area posed a risk to the public.
MAN CHARGED WITH MURDER OF MOTHER AND SISTER
A 26-year-old Wollongong man has been ordered to undergo a psychiatric examination after appearing in court charged with the murder of his mother and sister.
Ian Douglas McLeish, who is unemployed, appeared briefly in Wollongong Local Court today.
Police allege McLeish strangled his 54-year-old mother Elaine in the Dapto home after an argument, and 15 minutes later strangled his 24-year-old sister Kylie when she arrived home.
A short time later he called police.
They allege McLeish told them that he spent some time in a psychiatric hospital in November last year.
The defendant was remanded in custody to May the 20th.
FAN LETTER TO BRYANT INTERCEPTED
Queensland's Corrective Services Minister, Russell Cooper, has described four prisoners who tried to send a fan letter to mass murdered Martin Bryant, as the scum of the earth.
Mr Cooper says the letter, praising Bryant for the Port Arthur killings, was intercepted by authorities at the Sir David Longland prison near Brisbane.
Mr Cooper says the authors could face charges and extended sentences if they're identified by the Corrective Services Commission.
IN SPORT ...
Socceroo coach Terry Venables has named a 33-man squad for two trial matches later this month to decide the World Cup squad.
The squad for the Contenders series in Melbourne and Sydney consists of 13 local players and 20 overseas based Australians.
Venables says with national league finals, the Contenders matches and World Cup qualifiers taking place over the next 10 weeks, it's a crucial time for Australian soccer.
Meanwhile England's kept alive its hopes of qualifying for the World Cup after a two-nil win over Georgia at Wembley Stadium.
To tennis, and after 25 years the Australian Open has dropped its main sponsor from the tournament title.
The tournament will no longer be known as the Ford Australian Open falling into line with the three other grand slam events, the US Open, the French Open and Wimbledon.
But Ford, the Australian Open's major sponsor for the past 12 years, will remain as the main backer through to 2002.
Elsewhere, Australian player Sandon Stolle is through to the next round of the A-T-P tournament in Atlanta after defeating second seed Jonas Bjorkman 4-6, 7-6, 6-2 in their second round match.
The tournament's now lost its top three seeds - Chang, Bjorkman and Courier.
The Canberra Lakers head to Brisbane today for tomorrow night's National Hockey League semi-final against Perth.
Lakers coach Andrew Deane says his players are confident of causing an upset.
Canberra Cannons coach Brett Flannigan says he will give forward Chris Blakemore as much time as possible to prove his fitness for tomorrow night's NBL game against Brisbane.
Blakemore is battling an elbow injury.
And in the NBA playoffs, Chicago has won its Eastern Conference best of five series against Washington, three-nil.
The Bulls won today's game 96-95 with Michael Jordan scoring 28 points.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
